technique_name: C7.1 Discovery Platform Services > C7.1.4.1 Discovering Cloud Storage Objects
description:
An attacker could enumerate objects in the cloud storage infrastructure. An attacker can use this information during autodiscovery to shape subsequent behavior, including requesting all or specific objects from cloud storage. Similar to file and directory discovery on the local host, after determining available storage services (i.e., cloud infrastructure discovery), the attacker can access the content/objects stored in the cloud infrastructure.
Cloud service providers provide APIs that allow users to enumerate objects stored in cloud storage.
potential_defenses: "Restrict the permissions related to querying and accessing cloud storage objects, and only grant these permissions to necessary users."
Restrict permissions related to querying and accessing cloud storage objects
Secure cloud metadata service access
detection_opportunities: Abnormal queries on cloud storage services
Abnormal calls to enumeration APIs in cloud logs
code_examples_patterns: Query cloud storage enumeration APIs to list stored objects

technique_name: C7.1 Discovery Platform Services > C7.1.1.1 Accessing the Kubernetes API Server
description: After entering a pod, an attacker can directly access the Kubernetes REST API through curl or wget. With high-privilege service accounts, attackers can issue commands for lateral movement. Low-privilege accounts can still detect resource info, running status, and secrets in the cluster.
potential_defenses: Restrict service account permissions using RBAC
Rotate service account tokens regularly
Monitor API server access patterns
Secure pod-to-API server communication
detection_opportunities: Unusual API server access from pod contexts
Repeated namespace and pod enumeration via API calls
Abnormal token usage patterns in cloud logs
code_examples_patterns: Run 'cat ./run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token' to obtain token
Execute 'curl https://<apiserver>:443/api/v1/namespaces -H Authorization:Bearer <token> -k' to query cluster resources

technique_name: C7.1 Discovery Platform Services > C7.1.1.2 Accessing Kubelet APIs
description: In a Kubernetes cluster, each node runs Kubelet with APIs on ports 10250 (auth), 10255 (read-only, no auth), and 10256 (health check). The 10255 port allows unauthenticated read-only access to /pods, exposing node/pod addresses, mount status, and environment variables.
potential_defenses: Disable Kubelet read-only API (port 10255)
Enable authentication and authorization on Kubelet API
Restrict network access to Kubelet ports
Monitor cloud metadata service access
detection_opportunities: Unauthenticated access to Kubelet /pods endpoint
Repeated queries to cloud metadata service (169.254.169.254)
Abnormal curl commands targeting Kubelet ports from within containers
code_examples_patterns: Execute 'curl 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/local-ipv4' to obtain host IP
Access Kubelet read-only API: 'curl <node_ip>:10255/pods' to enumerate pod details

technique_name: C7.1 Discovery Platform Services > C7.1.1.3 Enter the pod where the K8s Dashboard is located

After entering a pod, attackers can scan the intranet to discover the Dashboard service address and authenticate using the kubernetes-dashboard service account. Container environment variables may also leak sensitive configuration.
potential_defenses: Restrict pod-to-pod network communication
Harden Kubernetes Dashboard authentication
Remove sensitive data from container environment variables
Monitor Dashboard access patterns
detection_opportunities: Internal scanning for Kubernetes Dashboard endpoints
Authentication attempts using service account tokens against Dashboard
Abnormal env command execution within containers
code_examples_patterns: Check for Docker: test -f /.dockerenv or grep docker /proc/1/cgroup
Run 'env' to enumerate container environment variables for leaked credentials

technique_name: C7.1 Discovery Platform Services > C7.1.1.4 Accessing K8s Service via NodePort

Execute 'curl <node_ip>:<nodeport>' to access Kubernetes services externally

technique_name: C7.1 Discovery Platform Services > C7.1.1.5 Unauthorized Access Exploiting etcd
description: etcd stores all Kubernetes cluster data. When misconfigured or combined with SSRF, unauthorized access to etcd is equivalent to taking over the entire cluster. Accessing https://etcd:2379/v2/keys/?recursive=true returns all stored keys in JSON format.
potential_defenses: Enable etcd authentication and TLS encryption
Restrict etcd network exposure to internal cluster only
Monitor etcd access logs for unauthorized queries
detection_opportunities: Unauthorized access to etcd endpoint on port 2379
Recursive key enumeration queries against etcd API
Abnormal netstat commands querying etcd connections
code_examples_patterns: Run 'netstat -pantu | grep etcd' to locate etcd endpoint
Access etcd: 'curl https://etcd:2379/v2/keys/?recursive=true' to dump all cluster data
